title: Synthetic trace fuzzer for sink compatibility and backpressure tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable synthetic trace generation and sink-fuzzing harness that exercises real downstream export paths (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party vendors) to validate format compatibility, graceful degradation, and backpressure behavior. The harness should be able to emit configurable trace envelopes (OTLP/gRPC, OTLP/http, Jaeger thrift/compact), variations (out-of-order spans, duplicated span IDs, missing parent references), compression modes, auth/credential permutations, and high-QPS bursts to trigger buffering and retry logic. The goal is to detect interoperability issues early, characterize failure modes under load, and create deterministic regression tests for exporter changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can emit traces to at least three sink types: Tempo HTTP, Tempo gRPC (OTLP), and a Jaeger-compatible endpoint.
2) Configurable scenarios supported: out-of-order spans, timestamp skew, duplicate spans, large-span payloads (>1MB), envelope fragmentation, and compressed payloads.
3) End-to-end test can simulate sustained burst traffic (configurable up to 10k spans/sec) and record sink-side responses, client-side error codes, and internal backoff metrics.
4) Test reports include deterministic golden outputs and diffs for format transformations and header handling.
5) Harness runs in CI as a nightly job against a lightweight testbed and as an on-demand local dev tool.
6) New exporter regressions must be covered by at least one fuzz scenario if they touch envelope or batching logic.
tasks: Design harness API and CLI: scenario descriptor format (YAML/JSON), sinks, auth configs, rate curves
Implement core generator that can synthesize valid span trees and inject corruption patterns (missing fields, truncated traces)
Add transport adapters: OTLP/grpc, OTLP/http/protobuf, Jaeger thrift over HTTP, and a generic HTTP sink shim
Implement burst/backpressure driver: configurable p99 spike, ramp-up/ramp-down, steady-state load
Capture and normalize sink responses: status codes, retry headers, rate-limit hints, and sampling rejections
Integrate with testbed: docker-compose stack with Tempo, Jaeger, and a mock-vendor sink that returns varied responses
Create CI job and nightly pipeline that runs a smoke matrix and stores artifacts (logs, envelopes, diffs) to S3
Author docs and quickstart for devs and SREs on how to run scenarios locally and interpret failures
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for generator invariants (span parent-child consistency, timestamps).
2) Integration smoke against local Tempo and Jaeger containers.
3) Regression suite that replays previously failing envelopes to ensure fixes.
4) Load experiments: run bursts at 1k, 5k, 10k spans/sec while measuring downstream latencies and exporter queue sizes.
5) Failure injection: mock-vendor returns 5xx, connection reset, TLS handshake failures, and observes our retry/backoff behavior.
6) Artifact collection: capture raw envelopes, sink responses, and our internal exporter metrics for triage.
rollout_plan:
Alpha: run manually with engineering testbed and collect feedback (1 week).
Beta: enable nightly CI job and a dashboard for failures (2 weeks).
GA: add scenario coverage to exporter PR merge gating and expose the CLI in the internal dev toolkit (4 weeks).
monitoring: Create dashboards: test-run success rate, scenarios failing by category, exporter queue depth during bursts, average sink error rate, and median sink response time. Add an alert for >3 failed scenarios in nightly run. Store artifacts in s3://redwood-observability/fuzz-artifacts/ENG-412350/
risks: High QPS synthetic traffic could consume dev/test cluster resources — schedule runs with quota and resource limits
Mock vendor behavior may diverge from production vendor semantics, leading to false negatives; mitigate by recording real vendor traces where possible
Test flakiness due to timing-sensitive scenarios — ensure determinism by seeding RNG and using fixed clocks where feasible
Sensitive data could accidentally be generated in payloads — generator must use synthetic, non-PII data
